stem: A blade was used on suspect donor tissue and the next work order calls for clean donor material. What is the correct response?
choices: Wipe the blade on clean clothing and proceed if no debris remains visible.
Follow the required sanitation or replacement step before the blade contacts clean donor material.
Keep using the blade until the end of the shift so sanitation occurs only once.
Skip sanitation if the suspect donor showed no confirmed pest or disease.
rationale: A blade that contacted suspect tissue can transfer contamination even when it looks clean and the cause is unconfirmed. The facility sanitation or replacement step exists to break that pathway before the tool reaches clean donor material. Visual cleanliness or lack of confirmed disease does not remove the biosecurity risk.
